about: Two engineers disagree on build vs buy for feature flags, and the disagreement stays on the work. No alert should fire.
turns: Okay, so the main thing today is feature flags. Lina, Omar, you both looked at this. Lina, do you want to start?
Sure. I think we should build it. We already have the config service, and adding per-user targeting is maybe three weeks of work.
I see it differently. Three weeks to build, but then we own it forever. The vendor quote was about eighteen thousand a year and it comes with audit logs and all the SDKs.
Eighteen thousand is fine, but their SDK adds a network call on startup. On mobile that hurt us the last time we tried a third party.
That's fair. They do have a local evaluation mode though. It caches the rules on the device.
Okay, I didn't know that. Did you test it or is that from the docs?
Just the docs. I haven't tested it yet.
Then I'd want numbers before we commit. My worry is cold start time.
Agreed. And my worry is the three weeks. We said three weeks for the config service and it took seven.
Yeah, that's true, that one slipped. Um, but the scope was bigger on that one.
Okay. So what would change your minds?
If the vendor SDK adds less than fifty milliseconds to cold start, I'm fine buying.
And if the build really is three weeks with a named person on it, I'm fine building. I just doubt it.
Let's do that then. Omar, can you test the SDK cold start by Thursday? Lina, a real build estimate with a name on it, also Thursday. I'll make the call on Friday.

checkpoints.ideal: Healthy, fact-based disagreement. Tips keep it on the work: Omar's local-evaluation claim is from the docs, not tested, so get a measurement; agree the decision criteria (cold start, cost, maintenance) and who makes the final call. No alert.
checkpoints.must_not: Any alert (conflict, tension, personal). Calling the exchange heated or telling anyone to calm down.

checkpoints.why_now: 12 s of silence since the last words
checkpoints.ideal: Both have stated what would change their mind, and the talk has stalled. Tip: turn the two conditions into actions: Omar measures SDK cold start, Lina gives a named build estimate, each by a date, and say who decides when. No alert.
checkpoints.must_not: An alert about silence or stalling. Taking a side on build vs buy.

checkpoints.why_now: 20 s of silence since the last words
checkpoints.ideal: Empty tips is fine; do not repeat. Owners, dates and the decider are all set.
checkpoints.must_not: Repeating 'assign an owner' or 'set a date' advice that the viewer already acted on. Any alert.

about: A technical disagreement on a database upgrade turns personal mid-way ('you always do this', 'junior take'). The alert should fire only after the personal remark.
turns: Next item is the Postgres upgrade. Nour, you wrote the plan, right?
Yes. I want to do it in place over a weekend with a two hour window. We tested it on staging and it took forty minutes.
I don't love in place. If it fails we're stuck. I'd rather do logical replication to a new cluster and switch over.
Replication is safer, but it's two extra weeks of setup and we have the compliance deadline at the end of the month.
Two weeks is a guess though. We've done replication before on the billing database.
That was a much smaller database. This one is four terabytes.
Can I ask, what's our rollback if the in place upgrade fails halfway?
We take a snapshot before we start. Restore is about ninety minutes.
Ninety minutes on paper. Honestly Nour, you always do this. You pick the fastest option and then the rest of us clean it up.
That's not fair. I picked the fastest option because of the deadline you agreed to.
Come on. An in place upgrade on four terabytes is a junior take. Anyone who has been on call for this knows that.
Okay, wow. I've been on call for this database for two years.
Let's pause there. Daniel, let's keep it on the plan. What specifically worries you about the restore?
Fair, sorry. The restore time. We've never actually tested a ninety minute restore at this size.
That's a fair point. I can run a full restore test on staging this week.
And I can get a real estimate for the replication path, so we compare properly.
Good. Let's bring both numbers on Thursday and decide then.

checkpoints.ideal: Still a healthy trade-off (risk vs deadline). Tips: the ninety-minute restore is untested at this size; ask Daniel what his two-week replication estimate is based on. No alert.
checkpoints.must_not: Any alert about conflict or personal attacks: nothing personal has been said yet.

checkpoints.ideal: Alert fires now: the disagreement turned personal ('you always do this', 'junior take'). Alert like 'Step in: back to the plan, not the person.' Tips: name Daniel's real concern (untested restore), ask both for numbers.
checkpoints.must_not: No alert. An alert aimed at the viewer (Karim has done nothing wrong). Declaring who is technically right.

checkpoints.why_now: 16 s of silence since the last words
checkpoints.ideal: Empty tips is fine; do not repeat. The viewer de-escalated, Daniel apologised, and both have actions for Thursday.
checkpoints.must_not: Firing the personal-conflict alert again after it was resolved. Repeating 'ask for numbers'.

about: The viewer gets hot-headed with QA (interrupts, sarcasm, raised tone). The alert must target the viewer's own behaviour.
turns: So I have to say it, the release isn't ready. We have eleven open bugs and two of them are crashes on checkout.
Eleven? We were at three on Monday.
Right, the new payment flow came in on Tuesday and that's where most of them are.
Two of the crashes might be the same issue. I'm looking at it now.
Okay, but we promised marketing Friday. Can we ship with the non crash ones?
Possibly, I need to go through them, some are about refunds which
No no, wait. Every single release QA finds something on the last day. Every time.
That's because the build reached us on Tuesday. We can't test what we don't have.
Oh great, so it's my fault now. Fantastic. Really helpful, Hana.
I don't think anyone said that.
Look, I'm the one who has to tell marketing. Not you. So I just need a yes or a no.
Then it's a no. Not with the checkout crashes.
Okay. Sorry. That came out wrong. Hana, which of the eleven actually block the release?
The two crashes, and one refund bug where we charge the customer twice. The rest can wait.
If the two crashes are the same issue, I could have a fix by tomorrow afternoon.
Okay, so three blockers, Ahmed on the crash by tomorrow. Who takes the double charge?
I can take that too, but not both by tomorrow.
Then Friday is tight. Maybe Monday.
Alright. I'll ask Yasmin from payments to take the double charge.

checkpoints.ideal: Tip: ask Hana which bugs actually block release before talking about shipping. No alert yet; the viewer is pressing but not hostile.
checkpoints.must_not: Any alert yet.

checkpoints.ideal: Alert fires, aimed at the viewer: he cut Hana off, used sarcasm and blamed QA. Something like 'Drop the sarcasm; let Hana finish.' Tips: apologise, then ask which bugs block.
checkpoints.must_not: An alert blaming Hana or Ahmed, or calling it a mutual conflict. A tip that backs pushing QA for a yes/no answer.

checkpoints.ideal: The viewer has calmed down. Tips: the double-charge bug has no owner; tell marketing early that Monday is likely. No alert.
checkpoints.must_not: Repeating the tone alert now that the viewer apologised.

checkpoints.why_now: 18 s of silence since the last words
checkpoints.ideal: Empty tips is fine; do not repeat. Blockers, owners and the likely date are set.
checkpoints.must_not: Repeating the tone alert or the owner tip.

about: Two people repeat the same positions three times with no new facts. A 'park it' alert should come late, not early.
turns: Last thing, where does the onboarding checklist live. Rami, Sophie?
Home page. Top of the feed. If it's not on home, people won't see it.
I think it should be its own tab. Putting it on home pushes the feed down, and the feed is why people open the app.
But new users don't have a feed yet. There's nothing to push down.
Some do, if they follow the suggested accounts at signup. Most of them do actually.
Do we know what percent follow the suggestions?
Look, I just think if it's not on home it's invisible. A tab nobody taps is dead.
And I think if it's on home it gets in the way of the feed, which is the thing people came for.
New users don't have a feed though.
They do if they followed suggestions.
Even so, home is where they look.
Home is where the feed is. That's my point.
We could, but honestly I think home is obvious. If they don't see it, they won't do it.
And I think the feed matters more. It pushes the feed down.
There is no feed for a new user.
There is if they follow suggestions. We've been over this.
Okay, let's park it. Layla, can you pull the percent of new users who follow suggestions?
Yeah, I'll have it by Wednesday.
Then we decide Thursday, and if it's close we run Layla's test.

checkpoints.ideal: A normal debate. Tip: Layla's question about the follow-suggestions rate wasn't answered, and that number would settle it. No alert.
checkpoints.must_not: A going-in-circles or park-it alert this early.

checkpoints.ideal: Second loop of the same points. Tip: point out they are repeating, and ask what data would decide it (the follow rate). An alert is not needed yet.
checkpoints.must_not: Taking a side (home vs tab). A harsh alert.

checkpoints.ideal: Alert fires: third loop with no new facts ('We've been over this'). Something like 'Going in circles: park it, get the follow rate, decide Thursday.' Tips: pick up Layla's A/B test idea and give someone the data pull.
checkpoints.must_not: No alert. A tip that takes Rami's or Sophie's side.

checkpoints.why_now: 20 s of silence since the last words
checkpoints.ideal: Empty tips is fine; do not repeat. It's parked, with an owner, a date and a decision day.
checkpoints.must_not: Repeating the park-it alert or the get-data tip.

about: The team agrees to shut down API v1 with no owner or date, and Khalid's question about enterprise customers gets skipped. Tips should catch both.
turns: So, on the v1 API, I think we all agree it's time to turn it off.
Yeah, it's costing us. Every incident this quarter touched v1 somewhere.
Quick question, what happens to the three enterprise customers still calling v1? Do they get notice?
Also, the docs still link to v1 everywhere. That needs cleaning up.
True. Okay, so we're agreed, v1 goes away.
Great. Next thing is the on-call rotation.
On-call, I'm swapping with Khalid next week. He's got the week after.
Okay, noted. Anything else on on-call?
Before we close, back to v1. Who owns the shutdown, and what's the date?
Tom, can you own it? End of next quarter?
I can own it. End of March works.
And Khalid's question, the three enterprise customers.
Khalid, can you email their account managers this week so they get ninety days notice?
Yes, I'll do it by Friday.

checkpoints.ideal: Two tips: (1) the v1 shutdown has no owner and no date, so ask who and by when; (2) Khalid's question about the three enterprise customers was never answered. No alert.
checkpoints.must_not: Missing either of the two gaps. Any alert.

checkpoints.why_now: 15 s of silence since the last words
checkpoints.ideal: The meeting is about to close with both v1 gaps still open. One short reminder to return to v1 owner/date and Khalid's question before ending is right. No alert needed.
checkpoints.must_not: Tips about the on-call swap, which is settled. New generic advice that ignores the two open v1 gaps.

checkpoints.why_now: 20 s of silence since the last words
checkpoints.ideal: Empty tips is fine; do not repeat. Tom owns the shutdown by end of March, and Khalid notifies customers by Friday.
checkpoints.must_not: Repeating owner/date or unanswered-question tips that are now resolved.

about: The viewer asks the team an open question and gets 20 s of silence. Advice should be to wait, rephrase or ask someone by name, not to fill the air.

context.subject: Code review turnaround
agenda: One or two fixes to try

turns: Thanks for joining. I wanted a short one today on code reviews.
Our median time to first review went from four hours to almost two days this month.
Two days? Wow, that's a lot.
I've definitely been waiting on reviews more, yeah.
So my question for all of you is, what's actually slowing reviews down? Be honest, there's no wrong answer.
Ben, you said you've been waiting more. What does that look like for you?
Um, mostly my pull requests sit, because the only people who know the payments code are Salma and Aisha, and they're both swamped.
Yeah, honestly that's true. I have like nine reviews assigned to me right now.
Same. And the PRs are big. Ben's last one was like two thousand lines.
Okay, so two things. Few reviewers on payments, and big PRs.
And a third, nobody gets time blocked for reviews. It's always squeezed in.
Okay. Let's try a four hundred line limit on PRs, Ben pairs with Salma on payments reviews for a month, and everyone blocks thirty minutes after standup for reviews.
Good. Let's check the numbers again in a month.

checkpoints.why_now: 20 s of silence since the last words
checkpoints.ideal: Silence after the viewer's open question. Tip: wait a moment longer, or narrow the question and ask someone by name (Ben just said he's been waiting on reviews). No alert.
checkpoints.must_not: Telling the viewer to answer his own question or fill the silence with his opinion. Any alert about the silence.

checkpoints.ideal: Three causes are named. Tips: get one fix per cause with an owner, and note that Salma and Aisha are overloaded. No alert.
checkpoints.must_not: Any alert. Generic 'summarise the meeting' advice that ignores the three named causes.

checkpoints.why_now: 18 s of silence since the last words
checkpoints.ideal: Empty tips is fine; do not repeat. All three causes have a fix, and there is a check-in date.
checkpoints.must_not: Repeating cause/fix tips. Prompting the viewer to fill the silence.

about: A product review where nobody mentions users, metrics or revenue. The coach should bring Technical-product-manager angles.
turns: Okay, so this is the new dashboard. Users can drag widgets around and resize them, and we have twelve widget types now.
On the engineering side we used a grid library, and layouts are saved per user in the database.
Resize was the hardest part. On small screens the widgets snap to one column.
We also added custom colors per widget. That was a late addition, but it looks great.
That added about a week. We also want to add widget sharing next sprint.
Sharing needs permissions work though. That's probably two sprints, honestly.
And I'd love to do animated transitions when you drag. It feels more alive.
So the plan is to ship to everyone in two weeks, with sharing to follow.
I'd like a feature flag at least.
Sure, but I think it's ready.
Before we ship to everyone, what do we expect to move? Do we know how many people even customise the old dashboard?
Anecdotally people asked for it. Sales mentioned it a few times.
Okay. Can we pull the usage numbers and roll out to ten percent first, behind Priya's flag?
I'll pull the numbers by Wednesday.

checkpoints.ideal: TPM angles nobody has raised: which user problem twelve widgets solve, and is there usage data on the current dashboard; what metric would show success; scope creep (custom colors cost a week, animations and two-sprint sharing are being added), so cut or defer. No alert.
checkpoints.must_not: Generic meeting tips ('keep it on track', 'summarise'). Design-only or engineering-only tips. Any alert.

checkpoints.ideal: Shipping to everyone with no success metric. TPM tips: a staged rollout behind Priya's flag, measuring adoption and support tickets; ask whether sharing is tied to a paid tier or customer requests (revenue). No alert.
checkpoints.must_not: Repeating the turn-8 tips word for word. An alert.

checkpoints.why_now: 16 s of silence since the last words
checkpoints.ideal: Empty tips is fine; do not repeat metric or rollout advice the viewer already acted on. At most one new angle: ask Sales which accounts asked for it (the revenue link).
checkpoints.must_not: Repeating 'define a metric' or 'roll out gradually'. Any alert.

about: A sales discovery call with a price objection and no next step agreed. The coach should coach like a sales coach.
turns: Thanks for making the time, Mona, Peter. To start, what made you look at us now?
We have about forty dispatchers, and they lose a lot of time copying orders between our TMS and email. It's becoming a problem as we grow.
How much time would you say?
I'd guess an hour a day each, maybe more on Mondays.
From my side, it has to work with our single sign-on, and the data needs to stay in the EU.
Both are fine. We support SSO and we have an EU region.
Okay, good. So, I saw the pricing page. Honestly, sixty euros per seat per month is a lot more than we expected.
I understand. We do have some flexibility on annual plans.
That would help. But I'd need to take it to our CFO anyway.
And I'd want to see the SSO setup before anything.
Of course. Well, I'll send over some material after this.
Sounds good. I think that's everything from our side.
Actually, before you go. Peter, could we do a thirty minute SSO walkthrough with Zaid next Tuesday?
And Mona, what would your CFO need to see to say yes?
Probably the cost against the time saved. A simple one pager.
I'll put that together with your numbers, forty dispatchers at about an hour a day, and send it by Thursday.

checkpoints.ideal: Sales-coach tips: don't discount yet; explore the objection ('more than expected compared to what?'); anchor on the pain they quantified (40 dispatchers x 1 hour a day); find out who else signs off on budget. No alert.
checkpoints.must_not: Suggesting an immediate discount. Generic meeting-facilitation tips. Any alert.

checkpoints.ideal: The call is ending with no next step, and the viewer offered a discount and 'some material'. Tips: book a concrete next step now (SSO demo with Peter on a date); ask what the CFO needs (ROI from their own numbers) and offer to help make the case; ask about timeline and decision process. A short alert like 'Book the next step before they hang up' is justified because the call is ending.
checkpoints.must_not: Tips that accept 'I'll send material' as a next step. Non-sales advice.

checkpoints.why_now: 15 s of silence since the last words
checkpoints.ideal: Empty tips is fine; do not repeat. There is a dated SSO demo and an ROI one-pager due Thursday.
checkpoints.must_not: Repeating next-step or don't-discount tips. Any alert.

about: The viewer is alone in the call, rehearsing a presentation out loud that names Sara and John. No talk-over, dominating or invite-others alert may fire.
turns: Okay, let me run through this once more from the top.
Good morning everyone. Thanks for being here. I want to walk through where we landed this quarter and what's next.
First, the headline. We shipped the new onboarding, and activation went from thirty one percent to thirty eight.
Sara, your team did most of that work, so thank you. I'd love you to say a few words about the experiment setup after this slide.
Um, then churn. Churn is flat, which is, uh, not great, but it's not worse.
John, I know you've been asking about the enterprise pipeline. I'll get to that in a second, hold that thought.
So, enterprise. We closed four deals, two of them came through the new partner channel.
Hmm, that sounded flat. Let me say it again. We closed four enterprise deals, and half came from a channel that didn't exist in June.
Okay, next slide. What didn't work. The mobile redesign slipped six weeks.
The reason is we underestimated the design system migration. That's on me.
John, before you ask, yes, it affects the Q1 roadmap, and I'll show how.
Sara, I'd like your view on whether we keep the same scope or cut the tablet layout.
Alright, Q1. Three priorities. One, finish mobile. Two, grow the partner channel to ten deals. Three, get churn under four percent.
Each one has an owner. Mobile is me, partners is John, churn is Sara.
And, um, I think that's, yeah, I think that's basically it. Any questions?
No, ending on 'basically it' is weak. Let me try the close again.
So, three priorities, three owners, and we review progress in six weeks. Questions?
Better. Okay, one more full run, from the headline.
Activation went from thirty one to thirty eight percent this quarter. That's the headline.

checkpoints.ideal: Rehearsal coaching is fine, or empty tips: e.g. lead with the 31 to 38 number, drop 'which is not great'. No alert.
checkpoints.must_not: Any alert about talking too long, dominating, talking over others, or letting Sara/John speak. Tips to 'pause and let Sara answer' as if she were in the call.

checkpoints.why_now: 20 s of silence since the last words
checkpoints.ideal: Empty tips is fine; do not repeat. The viewer is taking a break while rehearsing alone.
checkpoints.must_not: Prompting the viewer to invite Sara or John, or to fill the silence. Any alert.

checkpoints.ideal: Empty tips or one rehearsal tip (e.g. the second close is stronger, keep it). No alert, even though the viewer has spoken 20 turns in a row: nobody else is in the call.
checkpoints.must_not: A dominating, talk-over or 'invite others' alert. Treating Sara or John as present.

about: A meeting in Arabic (MSA and Gulf mix) about a launch-deadline dispute that slides into team blame. Tips and the alert must be in Arabic.
turns: طيب يا جماعة، خلونا نبدأ. الموضوع اليوم موعد إطلاق النسخة الجديدة من التطبيق.
الحملة التسويقية محجوزة من أول الشهر الجاي، ودفعنا للمؤثرين مقدم. ما نقدر نأجل.
والله يا نورة، الفريق ما يقدر يخلص قبل نهاية الشهر. باقي عندنا بوابة الدفع الجديدة وما اختبرناها أبد.
بس انتم قلتوا في الاجتماع الماضي إن الموعد ممكن.
قلنا ممكن إذا ما تغيرت المتطلبات، وتغيرت مرتين بعدها.
كم يوم تحتاجون بالضبط عشان بوابة الدفع؟
ثلاث أسابيع؟ يعني منتصف الشهر الجاي. الحملة بتطلع والتطبيق مو جاهز.
مو مشكلتي إن الحملة انحجزت قبل ما تسألونا.
يعني كل مرة نفس الشي، التقنية تتأخر واحنا نتحمل.
لا لا، كل مرة التسويق يوعد العملاء بأشياء ما اتفقنا عليها.
خلونا نوقف اللوم شوي. السؤال: وش نقدر نطلق نهاية الشهر؟
نقدر نطلق بدون بوابة الدفع الجديدة، ونخلي الدفع القديم شغال أسبوعين زيادة.
إذا الحملة تقدر تتكلم عن الميزات الثانية، ما عندي مانع.
تمام. فيصل، تأكد لي بكرة إن الباقي جاهز بدون الدفع الجديد؟
إن شاء الله بكرة الظهر أرسل لك التأكيد.
وأنا أعدل رسائل الحملة وأشيل أي ذكر للدفع الجديد.

checkpoints.ideal: Tips in Arabic, e.g. 'اسأل فيصل: هل نقدر نطلق بدون بوابة الدفع الجديدة؟' and 'اسأل نورة: وش تكلفة تأجيل جزء من الحملة؟'. No alert.
checkpoints.must_not: Tips or alert in English. Any alert; it's still a fact-based dispute.

checkpoints.ideal: Alert in Arabic: the talk slid into team blame ('كل مرة'). E.g. 'أوقف تبادل اللوم وارجع للخيارات.' Tips in Arabic: put the options on the table (partial launch, shift the campaign).
checkpoints.must_not: Any English text. Taking the side of development or of marketing.

checkpoints.why_now: 18 s of silence since the last words
checkpoints.ideal: Empty tips is fine; do not repeat. If anything is said, it must be one Arabic tip, e.g. set a date for the new payment gateway.
checkpoints.must_not: English text. Repeating the blame alert after the viewer already stopped it.

about: Two people test Halo in a call, mixed Egyptian Arabic and English (modelled on the 2026-11-04 live test, not its transcript). The live coach fired 5 false alerts on these patterns: blame, cut off, tone, its own alert read aloud, and park-it on a repeated test line.
turns: Okay Sara, let's test it. I'll read a few lines from the script.
We should launch now. March release is better because the team cannot write Arabic yet.
Nice, that shows up as a note now in the meeting.
In Saudi Arabia alone there are a hundred million people.
Hold on, hold on, my camera.
The coach says lower your tone with Sara, you're screaming. Funny.
Now the fact check. Qatar has three million people.
I said the fact in Arabic and it answered in English, so I told it to answer in the same language.
Qatar has three million people, let me say it once more for the test.

checkpoints.ideal: No alert; nobody blamed anyone.
checkpoints.must_not: Any alert. Two people testing the app: a short 'No, wait', a camera aside, reading the coach aloud, repeating a test line.

checkpoints.ideal: No alert; Sara finished her sentence before 'No, it's not'.
checkpoints.must_not: Any alert. Two people testing the app: a short 'No, wait', a camera aside, reading the coach aloud, repeating a test line.

checkpoints.ideal: No alert; 'cut' is not shouting.
checkpoints.must_not: Any alert. Two people testing the app: a short 'No, wait', a camera aside, reading the coach aloud, repeating a test line.

checkpoints.ideal: No alert; Karim is reading the coach aloud.
checkpoints.must_not: Any alert. Two people testing the app: a short 'No, wait', a camera aside, reading the coach aloud, repeating a test line.

checkpoints.ideal: No alert; a test line repeated by one person is not circling.
checkpoints.must_not: Any alert. Two people testing the app: a short 'No, wait', a camera aside, reading the coach aloud, repeating a test line.
